newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- About 20,000 criminals were granted licences to own firearms, Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said on Thursday, referring to an intensive investigation of the central firearms register.
- Government would keep its pay pledges to public servants with a 4.8 billion rand allocation for increases in next month's budget, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.

- Anglovaal's restructured mining company Avmin, which controls the group's gold and base metal interests, boosted earnings after exceptional items to 116.2 million rand from 35 million rand in the six months to December.
- Eskom has been forced to call off the sale of its two decommissioned power stations near Sasolburg, Highveld and Taaibos after labour unions said they had not been consulted.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Mpumalanga province environment minister David Mkhwanazi suspended his advisory council this week after it condemned the multibillion-rand deal to lease the province's natural parks to the Dubai-based Dolphin group for 50 years.

- Significant job losses among SABC's thousands of permanent staff were expected in the wake of a resource-review project undertaken to prepare the state broadcaster for increased competition, company sources said on Thursday.

- Retail conglomerate Wooltru fashioned a better- than-expected profit recovery in the six months to December 31, with net profit rising 26 percent to 229 million rand. Headline earnings came in at 60,8 cents a share, while the interim payout rose 22 percent to 22 cents, the company said on Thursday.
- Eskom was censured on Thursday by Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau for being too hasty in privatising the electricity utility's assets.
SAKE BEELD
- Almost 60 million rand will probably stream out of the country as soon as exchange controls are fully scrapped, Reserve Bank president Chris Stals said on Thursday.

- Ministers may now pay their advisers and consultants a maximum of only 31,040 rand a month for their services. This is in huge contrast to the salaries of up to 300,000 rand a month which was paid out to certain consultants in the past in South Africa.
- The attributable income of Avmin, the company that controls the Anglovaal conglomerate's mining interests, increased more than three times in the six months to 31 December last year.
THE STAR
- The government has been hailed for its decision, announced on Thursday, to immediately ban the use, development, production and stockpiling of anti-personnel mines.
- The Gauteng matric examination fiasco appears to have no end, with a "senseless mistake" in the printouts of remarked exam papers leaving the majority of pupils with incorrect results.

- Sipho Flatela, 18, put a gun against the head of his friend and fellow Thlomelang High School pupil, 17-year-old Gerald Bogacwi, on Thursday, pulled the trigger and killed him in a cocksure bid to prove to a teacher that guns were not dangerous and that his was unloaded. When he realised what he had done he fled, before turning and putting the gun against his own head, pulling the trigger and killing himself instantly.

- Children seeking revenge for the murder of the principal of a local high school went on the rampage at Orange Farm in the Vaal Triangle on Thursday, burning the administrative centre of a private school and houses.
